report.source_text: The infant was weaned to room air and continued to improve on oral feeds. By the time of discharge, the infant was taking most of the feeds orally. The infant was discharged on room air and oral hydrochlorothiazide-spironolactone 3 mg, given the VSD with the pulmonary over-circulation. Oral phenobarbital 20 mg/5 mL, oral levetiracetam 100 mg/mL, and oral lacosamide 10 mg/mL were continued for seizure management with the Neurology Department.

clinician.final_diagnosis: De novo heterozygous variant at c. 2771 G>A of the Col4a1 gene
clinician.trajectory_summary: A male infant born at 38 weeks with prenatal findings of microcephaly, multifocal brain infarcts, polymicrogyria, and cardiac anomalies was admitted with dusky, cool extremities, limpness, and seizures. Postnatal exams and imaging confirmed CNS anomalies (multifocal infarcts, polymicrogyria, corpus callosum dysgenesis) and cardiac defects (fenestrated atrial septum, VSD, hypoplastic left ventricle and aortic arch, PDA). Genetic testing revealed a de novo heterozygous c. 2771 G>A variant in the Col4a1 gene, correlating with multisystem findings. Seizures required multiple antiepileptic agents with eventual control. The infant improved clinically, weaned to room air, and was discharged on oral medications including diuretics and antiepileptics.

Postnatal physical exam demonstrated dusky feet, cool extremities, limpness, and respiratory support requirements
Postnatal brain MRI confirmed multifocal infarcts, polymicrogyria, corpus callosum dysgenesis, optic nerve hypoplasia
Postnatal echocardiography revealed fenestrated atrial septum, muscular VSD, hypoplastic left ventricle and aortic arch, PDA, elevated right ventricular pressures
Genetic testing confirmed de novo heterozygous variant c.2771 G>A of the Col4a1 gene
Seizures were difficult to control initially, requiring multiple intravenous antiepileptic therapies with later EEG showing no seizures
Clinical course showed improvement with weaning to room air and feeding by mouth; discharge on oral diuretics and antiepileptics
